checklist.description: Extract the existing terminal keyboard event helpers from the 2,958-line toolbar.js into a cohesive src/surfaces/web/static/js/features/terminal-keyboard.js, preserving existing behavior and helper interfaces. Keep renderer lifecycle and input transport in toolbar.js and clipboard operations in terminal-clipboard.js. Load the module before toolbar.js in index.html and update the explicit loaders in tests/support/terminal_clipboard_runtime.js, tests/web_supervisor_toolbar.test.js, and tests/web_goal_log_tail.test.js.

Extend the shared xterm custom-key handler to recognize non-composing keydown events for Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown without Ctrl, Shift, or Meta. For the focused, active, current renderer, prevent the browser default and suppress xterm's duplicate encoding; enqueue ESC[1;3A or ESC[1;3B through queueTerminalInput only when the originating session remains usable. Consume matching input without sending it after exit or session loss. Preserve renderer/session fencing and emit once per keydown, including deliberate repeat. Apply consistently across terminal profiles and providers; leave other key combinations to existing handlers and xterm.

Add focused keyboard-policy tests and tests/web_terminal_keyboard_browser.test.js using the existing browser fixture and actual vendored xterm. Assert exact input-route bytes for Alt+Up/Down under Linux, Windows, and macOS platform settings in normal and application cursor modes. Cover repeat, keyup, extra modifiers, composition, outside focus, retained/exited output, tab switching, renderer replacement, and session replacement before flush. Verify profile/provider consistency and preserve ordinary/Ctrl arrows, Alt+Left/Right, Ctrl+Enter, Agent-versus-shell Ctrl+Z, clipboard behavior, and palette precedence. Require the real-browser regression to fail on the pinned baseline; the VM's simplified encoder cannot prove xterm behavior.

Update only docs/intent/05-surfaces/03-browser/19-terminal.md to document focused Alt+Up/Down modifier preservation across shared terminal profiles, with the attached application retaining ownership of shortcut behavior. Keep implementation details and provider-specific conversation actions out of the product contract.

Then run the full tests/*.test.js suite with that NODE_PATH, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test --lib --bins -- --test-threads=1, cargo build --release --locked, and git diff --check. Compare any broader failures against pinned baseline 0b6cc819de716b1b118f40c4465d114290117699 by exact failure identity. Report byte-level verification separately from any native Codex smoke test; do not deploy or restart the supervising installation.

result.summary: workflow.plan.enter:default-plan: Restore native Alt+Up delivery through the shared terminal keyboard adapter. The bundled xterm rewrites Alt+Up to Ctrl+Up on non-macOS platforms; the backend forwards those incorrect bytes unchanged. The governing invariant is that focused terminal navigation preserves the user's modifiers and reaches only its originating session. Ownership remains in the browser terminal adapter, with shortcut meaning owned by the attached CLI. Use a focused reproduction-and-regression approach. Correct Alt+Down alongside Alt+Up because both share the demonstrated vertical-arrow remapping. Prefer the existing custom-key hook over modifying vendored xterm, changing platform detection, rewriting backend input, or adding Codex-specific behavior. Changing terminalKeyData alone would miss the production xterm path. Keep Model, Application, Infrastructure, and workflow contracts unchanged.

checklist.evidence: Extracted keyboard policy into the 97-line terminal-keyboard.js. All four existing helpers match the baseline byte-for-byte. Updated index.html and all three explicit test loaders. Renderer lifecycle, transport, and clipboard operations retain their existing owners.

The shared custom-key hook consumes focused, non-composing Alt+Up/Down keydowns and queues ESC[1;3A/B once per event, including repeat. Exited or missing sessions consume the gesture without sending. Browser tests verify renderer and session fencing.

Added five policy tests and 13 real Chromium/xterm tests covering platform settings, cursor modes, repeats, keyup, composition, modifiers, focus, retained output, lifecycle changes, profiles/providers, neighboring shortcuts, and palette precedence. The regression fails on the pinned Linux and Windows baseline because Alt+Up emits ESC[1;5A.
Updated only docs/intent/05-surfaces/03-browser/19-terminal.md to document modifier preservation and attached-application shortcut ownership.

Focused and full web suites pass without skips. Rust tests, formatting, locked release build, and whitespace checks pass. Baseline full web suite also passes; no broader failure comparison was needed.

skill.name: Quality
skill.prompt:
## Quality review

Independently review the finalized plans and candidate implementation. Select or add meaningful tests, correct defects when needed, and run the relevant checks. Report actual commands, results and findings. Refine verifies the exact candidate and supervises evaluation commands.

## Required behavior

Preserve the relevant Goal and docs/intent product behavior. Keep Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces coherent; shared capabilities authoritative; local state and evidence inspectable and recoverable; and affected surfaces semantically consistent.

## Review and verification

Judge the candidate against the Goal and only the relevant docs/intent pages. Use the smallest deterministic checks that cover the affected behavior, adding or adjusting behavior-focused tests only when evidence is missing. Scale integration and failure-path checks to actual risk. Test the governing invariant through the affected real entry paths and lifecycle boundaries. Look for cases that could disprove the implementation's assumptions, including relevant callers outside the changed files. Group findings with a common cause into one coherent recovery request. Report exact commands, results, and remaining uncertainty. Do not require unrelated tests, documentation, refactors, or cleanup; documentation is relevant only when product intent or an architectural contract changes.

## Acceptance checks

- The candidate satisfies the Goal and relevant docs/intent contracts, preserves the existing architecture and consistent behavior across affected surfaces, and passes focused deterministic regression checks.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
